title: Volume & Capacity
subtitle: Space taken up, and space available to fill.
objectives: Name the standard units of each
Explain why 1 mL and 1 cm³ are the same size
Estimate a volume in sensible units

cards.title: Volume and capacity are not quite the same word
cards.text: Volume is how much space something takes up. Capacity is how much a container can hold. Usually close, never identical.

cards.title: One is about the thing, one about the space inside it
cards.text: A mug has both, and they are different numbers.
points: **Volume of the mug** includes the ceramic walls.
**Capacity of the mug** is only the hollow.
**A solid brick has volume** and essentially no capacity.
**Both are measured in the same units**, which is why they get muddled.

question.explain: It takes up space, so it has volume. Nothing can be poured into it, so capacity is essentially zero.

cards.title: Cubic for solids, litres for liquids
cards.text: Two families, one bridge between them.
points: **Volume:** cubic centimetres (cm³) and cubic metres (m³).
**Capacity:** millilitres (mL) and litres (L).
**1 mL is exactly 1 cm³.** That is the bridge.
**1 L is 1,000 cm³.** Which is a 10 × 10 × 10 box.

cards.title: Volume outruns the edge it grows from
cards.text: A 10 cm cube holds exactly one litre. Press 1, 2, 3, 4 and see how fast the volume climbs.

question.text: How many cubic centimetres are in 1 litre? Digits only.
question.explain: A litre is a 10 × 10 × 10 cm box: 1,000 cm³.

cards.title: A fan moves volume, and it is measured
cards.text: The box says something like 60 m³ per minute. That is how much air it shifts.
points: **Cubic metres**, because air is counted in big volumes.
**60 m³ a minute** would fill a small bedroom in about a minute.
**Bigger blades move more volume**, not faster air.
**Airflow is a volume rate**, not a speed.

cards.title: Pick the unit that keeps the number sensible
cards.text: If you need lots of zeros or lots of decimals, you have chosen the wrong unit.
points: **A spoon** of medicine. Millilitres.
**A water bottle**: litres.
**A room**: cubic metres.
**A grain of rice**: cubic millimetres.

cards.title: Pick the unit that keeps it sensible
cards.alt: A one-litre jug, a half-litre bottle, a small cup, a tablespoon and a syringe lined up by size
cards.text: A syringe in litres is silly. A water drum in millilitres is worse.

cards.title: Minecraft is literally built out of cubic metres
cards.text: One block is a metre on each side. So a block is one cubic metre, and counting blocks is measuring volume.
points: **Double every side** and it is 8,000, not 2,000.
**That is the cube** doing its work again.
**Mining out a room** is a volume calculation you already do.

question.text: Which unit suits the volume of a classroom?
question.explain: Cubic metres. Using cm³ would need a seven-digit number.

cards.title: Rainfall is reported in a strange unit
cards.text: '200 mm of rain' is a depth, not a volume. The volume depends on the area it fell on.
points: **200 mm over one square metre** is 200 litres.
**Over a hectare** it is two million litres.
**That is why** a number that sounds small floods a city.
**Depth × area = volume.** Always ask over what area.

terms.def: The amount of space an object takes up.
The amount a container can hold.
The space in a 1 cm by 1 cm by 1 cm cube; equal to 1 mL.
1,000 cm³, the volume of a 10 cm cube.

cards.title: Volume and capacity, in one pour
cards.alt: Water poured from a clear cube-shaped container into a tall jug, caught mid-pour
cards.text: The cube has a volume. The jug has a capacity. The water is the same either way.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Volume is space taken; capacity is space available.
1 mL = 1 cm³. That bridge connects both families.
1 L = 1,000 cm³ = a 10 cm cube.
Choose the unit that keeps the number readable.

options: how much a container can hold
quiz.explain: Capacity is about what fits inside.
They are the same size by definition. That is the bridge between the two unit families.

quiz.text: How many cm³ in 1 litre? Digits only.

quiz.explain: It occupies space but cannot be filled.

quiz.text: Best unit for a dose of cough syrup?
quiz.explain: Millilitres keep the number small and sensible.

quiz.text: Best unit for the air in a bedroom?
quiz.explain: Cubic metres. Anything smaller needs too many digits.

quiz.text: Volume and capacity are measured in different units entirely.
quiz.explain: They share units, which is exactly why the words get confused. 1 mL is 1 cm³.

quiz.text: A litre is the volume of a cube with edges of…
A fan rated at 60 m³ per minute is describing…
options: how much air it shifts each minute
quiz.explain: Airflow is a volume rate: how much, not how fast.

quiz.text: 200 mm of rain falling on one square metre is about…
quiz.explain: Depth times area. 0.2 m × 1 m² = 0.2 m³, which is 200 litres.

quiz.text: How many mL in 2.5 litres? Digits only.
quiz.explain: Each litre is 1,000 mL, so 2.5 litres is 2,500 mL.

quiz.text: Why does 'mm of rain' not tell you the volume?
options: It is a depth, so you need the area as well
quiz.explain: Volume needs depth and area together.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 6 Math, the first of three weeks on volume and capacity. The two words are separated at the start because they share units, which is the reason they get muddled, and a solid object is used to make the distinction concrete. The mL-equals-cm³ bridge is taught as the single fact that joins the two unit families, and the litre is anchored to a 10 cm cube so it has a size rather than being a word. The rainfall card is included because 'mm of rain' is a depth he will meet every typhoon season and almost nobody explains it.
discussion: What is the difference between volume and capacity?
Why is 1 mL the same as 1 cm³?
What does 200 mm of rain actually mean?
extension: Find a 10 cm cube-ish container and check it holds about a litre.
Look up the airflow rating on a fan at home.
misconceptions: That volume and capacity are the same thing.
That a litre has no physical size.
That mm of rain is a volume.
